newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Mining giants queue to buy ZCCM assets.
newsitem.headline: Mining giants queue to buy ZCCM assets.

text.p: The Zambia Privatisation Agency said on Friday that it expected the world's leading mining houses to be among companies that had put in bids for Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) assets.
"We expect the big companies that pre-qualified for the sale of ZCCM units to be among those that bid," a ZPA spokesman said hours before the bids were opened in the Zambian capital.
A total of 38 companies pre-qualified for the sale of ZCCM units including firms from South Africa, the United States, Canada, Australia, China, India, Belgium, Britain, Japan and Zambia itself.
Among the pre-qualifiers are two consortia -- led by Avmin Ltd, the minerals division of South African mining house Anglovaal Ltd, and Zambia Copper Investments, a unit of Anglo American Corp Ltd.

Both groups prequalified for the purchase of eight of the 10 units being put up for sale, including "Package A" which includes the prized Nchanga and Nkana divisions which together account for more than half of current copper production.

The consortia are also bidding for Luanshya Division, the Mufulira Underground Mine and Concentrator, the Chambishi Copper Mine, the Kansanshi Copper Mine, the Nampundwe Pyrite Mine, the Chambishi Cobalt Plant, and the Ndola Precious Metals Plant.

Other major players pre-qualifing for substantial interest in the company included Gencor Ltd, Falconbridge Ltd, The Broken Hill Propriety Company Ltd, Caledonia Mining Corp, Noranda Inc, Phelps Dodge Corp, Iscor Ltd, Teck Corp, Western Mining Corp, China Non-Ferrous Metals Industry Corp and Metorex.
The ZPA said not all pre-qualifiers made final bids for the assets.
"For example, about half of the pre-qualifiers for Kansanshi mine did not made final bids for it," the spokesman said.
